title: QUIC RFC 9000 Stream Priority Runtime Verification
verification_method: Requirement-home execution, packet-order inspection, benchmark validation for the priority-sorted flush path, SpecTrace render/check, and canonical JSON validation.
scope: This verification covers local-only stream priority storage and priority-aware ordering of queued application sends on the active runtime. It does not cover wire-level prioritization exchange, HTTP/3 priority trees, candidate-path scheduling, or multipath behavior.
expected_result: Requirement-home tests prove that writable streams can store and retrieve a local priority value, higher-priority queued writes flush before lower-priority queued writes, equal priorities preserve FIFO order, and no new prioritization frame appears on the wire. The permanent benchmark suite exercises the delayed-write priority comparison path without claiming a stable performance baseline.
procedure: Run the focused RFC 9000 S2P3 requirement-home tests.
Run the priority-sort benchmark suite with BenchmarkDotNet Dry validation and preserve the generated BenchmarkDotNet artifacts.
Render and check the touched SpecTrace artifacts.
preconditions: The runtime has a validated active path and can queue delayed application sends.
The tested streams have writable sides so their local priority controls are meaningful.
The packet-opening helper can inspect protected 1-RTT packet payloads for frame ordering.

supplemental_sections.heading: Packet Inspection Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The proof should inspect the protected application packet bytes after opening them with the existing handshake coordinator so the test can verify stream-frame order without inventing a new packet format.

supplemental_sections.heading: Benchmark Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The benchmark evidence is an internal Incursa-only queue-ordering comparator suite. It is not a public facade, System.Net.Quic, MSQUIC, HTTP/3, or interop comparison.

status_summary: Passed for the local-only stream-priority slice over the existing queued application send path. Focused requirement-home tests proved the no-wire-exchange floor, the public stream priority round-trip, and the priority-aware queued-send ordering floor; the permanent queue-ordering benchmark suite was added as internal performance evidence and validated with a BenchmarkDotNet Dry run on 2026-05-03. The 2026-05-10 S2P3 traceability topoff also passed: focused S2P3-0001 requirement-home filter 1/1, focused S2P3-0003 requirement-home filter 1/1, regenerated QUIC coverage triage marks REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S2P3-0001 and REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S2P3-0003 trace_clean and reports 1,523 of 1,771 QUIC requirements trace-clean overall, SpecTrace core validation passed for 535 artifacts, and git diff --check passed with only generated-triage CRLF normalization warnings. This verification does not claim wire-level prioritization, HTTP/3 dependency trees, candidate-path scheduling, multipath behavior, or public API widening.
